To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HIV‐1 CRFs are emerging in Estonia, and that they are resistant to antiretroviral drugs.

HIV‐1 subtype CRF06_cplexperienced patients have developed additional NRTI mutations, especially the ddIM184V and L74IV mutations, and several additional NNTRI mutations, after the failure of first‐line NNTRI + two NRTI regimens.
HIV‐1 CR06_cpx viruses after the failure of first line NNRTIs containing regimens develop additional NRTIs and NNRTIs mutations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a number of important issues in HIV‐1 infection.
the study of HIV‐1 drug resistant mutations (DRMs).
the study of the prevalence and distribution of drug resistance mutations among the first line treatment failed patients infected with HIV CRF06_cx.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
after the failure of first‐line NN RTI + NNRTI treatment regimen in CRF06_cxx HIV‐1 infected patients in Estonia, viruses develop more DRMs compared with the subtype B HIV‐1.
the NNRTI class of antiretrovirals should not be used in treatment naïve patients infected with CRF06_cox.
the usage of EFZ + 3TC + ZDV in this subtype is a more preferable first‐line therapy compared to EFZ + 2 NRTIs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the usage of efavirenz and lamivudine with didanosine in treatment naïve patients infected with subtype B or CRF06_cph viruses should be avoided, as it is associated with the development of additional drug resistance mutations.
the prevalence of drug resistance mutations is high among the HIV‐infected subjects in Estonia.

the prevalence of drug resistance mutations among the HIV‐infected individuals in Estonia is high, and the usage of ddI in the first line treatment regimens decreases the options for subsequent treatment regimens.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the usage of EFZ + 3 TC + ZVD regimen in treatment of HIV‐1 CR06_cpx infected patients is associated with a lower risk of developing NRTI and especially NNRTI DRMS compared to EFV +3 TC + ddI therapy.
the failure of the EFV + 3TC + ddI regimen is more common among the CRF06_cpix infected patients in comparison to the subtype B infected individuals.

HIV‐1 CR6_cpx infected patients have a high frequency of drug resistant mutations (DRMs), and the usage of EFZ + 3TC + ddI regimen in this subtype may decrease the options for next line regimens containing abacaivir and NNRTIs class agents.
